title: Plato's Cave
summary: In Book VII of the Republic, Plato has Socrates describe prisoners chained in a cave since childhood, able to see only shadows cast on a wall by objects carried in front of a fire behind them. One prisoner is freed, turns to see the fire, and is dragged up into the sunlight, where he slowly learns to see real things and finally the sun itself. When he returns to free the others, his eyes are useless in the dark, and they mock him. Plato uses the image for education, for the difference between appearance and reality, and for the philosopher's duty to go back down.
